Do A and B name the same business concept (the same real-world thing, so the classes model one concept under different names)? Concepts that merely share attributes such as an id or a date are not the same.

### A

response.rationale: A and B are different concepts. A, the Treatment Product, is a catalogue item: TreatmentProductRepository stores TreatmentProductRecord entries ("private readonly items = new Map<string, TreatmentProductRecord>();"), and TreatmentService.addProduct and listProducts call it. B, the Treatment, is an event applied to a particular hive: ReportService looks treatments up by hive ("for (const t of this.treatments.findByHive(hive.id))"). The graph backs this up. ReportService calls two separate repositories, TreatmentRepository.findByHive and TreatmentProductRepository.findAll, so the code treats them as two things. A treatment probably refers to a product, but the product and the act of applying it are not the same real-world thing.
